newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after bonds rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after bonds rise.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Sunday as yields on inflation-linked bonds extended their fall, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.08 percent, or 3.23 points, to 301.97 on a moderate all-share turnover of 175 million shekels against 185 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.49 percent higher at 308.15.

"The main reason for the strong rise of the market is the recent rise in the prices for CPI-linked long bonds," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments. "Yields on these bonds fell to less than four percent and they are expected to continue falling."

"Falling bond yields will send more money into the stock market. Moreover, the government is expected to issue fewer bonds in the near term and many saving plans expire this month. Some of this money will eventually find its way to the market," Finn said.

In its weekly report, First International Bank of Israel recommended that clients selectively increase their portfolios' equities weighting. It said share prices would continue rising as mutual funds attracted new money and bond yields continued falling.
"Investors are very optimistic and the market looks good. After the index lost almost two percent on Thursday the market is ready to rise again," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
"Even an attempt by Maof options speculators to push the market downwards today failed," Rosenfeld added.

Formula Systems gained 2.75 percent to 6,518 agorot. Carnegie Emerging Markets initiated coverage of Formula with a strong buy recommendation, saying the stock remained significantly undervalued despite a doubling in price in the past year.
Carnegie said Formula's earnings per share would reach 7.34 shekels in 1997 and 7.72 shekels in 1998 from 3.08 shekels in 1996. It set a six-month price target of 85 shekels for the shares.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.25 percent to 22,594 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which rose 2.75 percent to 580 agorot on turnover of 9.2 million shekels; and Israel Discount Bank, which gained 2.0 percent to 384 agorot on volume of 8.4 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
